items.title: From a polynomial relation with coefficients in R, the leading coefficient times t is integral
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Given a ring map from R to S and an element t of S satisfying a polynomial relation with R-coefficients a_0, ..., a_n the lemma produces an integral element, namely a_n t (statement lines 30697-30703). The proof does not invoke determinants, Cayley-Hamilton or the module of symmetric powers: it multiplies the relation by the (n-1)-st power of the leading coefficient and redistributes the powers of a_n among the terms so that the equation becomes monic in a_n t (proof lines 30705-30713). The exact bookkeeping of that rescaling, especially that the top term becomes the n-th power of a_n t, is the content, and the author writes the whole computation out. H2.
